Tomorrow is going to be a historic day.

Market expectations for tomorrow's Fed decision are among the most divided in recent history.

Currently, interest rate futures imply a ~30% chance of a rate hike and a ~70% chance of rates remaining unchanged.

By comparison, nearly every Fed meeting since March 2020 has entered decision day with ~99% consensus.

Adding to the uncertainty, Fed Chair Warsh has effectively eliminated forward guidance, leaving markets with little direction ahead of the announcement.

That said, we continue to believe that the Fed will NOT hike interest rates tomorrow.

It's important to not forget that just months ago, President Trump said a "pre-condition" for his next Fed Chair was a willingness to cut rates.

And, the Iran War energy shock is likely to continue being labeled as a "temporary inflationary event" rather than a structural one, the labor market is weak, and Americans are already struggling with high interest rates.

We think the Fed PAUSE continues tomorrow.

The AI Revolution is dividing the software industry:

The US Infrastructure Software Index and the US Security Software Index are up +22%, year-to-date, outperforming other parts of the industry.

At the same time, the US Vertical Software Index and the US Application Software Index are down -28% and -34%, respectively.

This brings the broad US Software Index down to -13% year-to-date.

This comes as the AI boom is driving unprecedented demand for cloud infrastructure, data centers, and the cybersecurity software needed to protect them, boosting infrastructure and security companies.

Meanwhile, application and vertical software companies are under pressure as investors fear AI will automate more tasks, reduce demand for traditional software licenses, and lower switching costs, making it easier for customers to change providers.

The AI software trade is becoming increasingly fragmented.

For folks who genuinely believe you need a URSF to reject every soft fork proposal, just think about how fragile that is.

Some dude on the internet wants a new OP code --> we have to notice and code a URSF.

A government wants to restrict all transactions to halt the network --> we'd need to code up a URSF.

The whole crux of Bitcoin being resistant to change, is that the default answer to all fork proposals is NO, and the default behaviour of doing nothing literally resists all proposed changes.
